body:
Redis限流器`redisRateLimitHandler`处理逻辑有bug：
当`ModelRequestRateLimitCount = 0`时，会直接报429错误，并不会忽略。
预期应该是max为0值时忽略（根据输入框提示文本说明理解的：“包括失败请求的次数，0代表不限制”）。
简单加个判断即可，我已经验证符合需求。

> 另外内存限流器`memoryRateLimitHandler`测试结果符合预期，不用处理。

------

Redis rate limiter `redisRateLimitHandler` has a bug in its processing logic:
When `ModelRequestRateLimitCount = 0`, it directly reports a 429 error and is not ignored.
The expected behavior should be to ignore when max is 0 (understood from the input box prompt text: "Includes the number of failed requests, 0 means no limit").
Simply adding a check will suffice, I have verified it meets the requirements.

> Additionally, the memory rate limiter `memoryRateLimitHandler` test results are as expected and do not need to be handled.

body:
This adds configurable options in the .json file for:

- "enableJit"
    - Specifies whether the JIT should be enabled. It must be enabled by default.
- "enableMainRamICache"
    - Specifies whether the instruction cache should be enabled on main ram.
- "enableIWramDCache"
    - Specifies whether the data cache should be enabled on IWRAM.
    
According to some tests by @Dartz150  and me, enabling the IWRAM data cache breaks certain games. We may need to investigate this on a per-game basis, or I might be missing something in how it should be properly configured.

Please feel free to ping me on Discord if you'd like to review it together!

#### 9bcfc6eb9f1504539c3be7638d739c0047a2802c 
[JSC] Add numeric hot loop unrolling pattern
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=292521
rdar://150660479

Reviewed by Yusuke Suzuki.

This patch introduces a specialized unrolling pattern for "numeric hot loops" — loops
that are dominated by numeric computation and local variable access, and which are not
expected to be inlined due to their size.

Key changes:
- Introduced a new unrolling heuristic for loops where:
  - Only one non-pad block exists in the loop,
  - More than 30% of material nodes are numeric computation nodes,
  - More than 40% are local access nodes,
  - The material node count is between 160 and 225.

Since FTL inlining is governed by the total function size
(`maximumFunctionForCallInlineCandidateBytecodeCostForFTL`, currently 170),
loops with body sizes above 160 are unlikely to be inlined. Therefore, unrolling
them doesn't harm inlining decisions but may still yield performance benefits.

Additional changes:
- Added `isNumericComputationNode()` and `isLocalAccessNode()` helpers.
- Introduced `MaxNumericHotLoopSize = 225` as the special-case upper bound.
- Refactored `maxAllowedUnrollSize()` to reflect both general and special-case limits.
- Ensured early bailout during loop scanning uses the updated size limit.

This change improves performance on tight computational loops that were previously
skipped due to general unroll thresholds, while avoiding regressions in code size

feat: Add weekly workout planning, logging, dashboard metrics & visualisation

Summary:
---------
This commit introduces functionality for:
- Setting and saving weekly workout goals.
- Logging individual workout sessions (type, duration, calories).
- Viewing weekly summaries and progress in the user dashboard.
- Visualising data through interactive charts using Chart.js.

Features:
---------
- Added workout goal entry form (`workout_plan.html`)
- Added workout logging page (`input.html`)
- Enhanced dashboard:
  • Displays latest weekly goals
  • Sums total calories and time
  • Lists all workouts by type
- Visualisation page (`visualise.html`):
  • Line chart: calories burnt per weekday
  • Pie chart: workout type breakdown
  • Progress bars: weekly goal vs actual

Backend:
---------
- Introduced new `Workout` model (user_id, workout_type, duration, calories_burnt, timestamp)
- Updated `/dashboard`, `/input`, and `/visualise` routes in `app.py`
- Passed data to templates for visualisation
- JSON-encoded data for Chart.js rendering

Testing:
---------
- Logged workouts and verified data appears in dashboard + charts
- Confirmed edge cases (no plan, no workouts) handled gracefully
- Verified session protection on all new pages

Files Added/Updated:
---------------------
• app.py
• database.py
• templates/dashboard.html
• templates/workout_plan.html
• templates/input.html
• templates/visualise.html

Next Steps:
------------
- Add edit/delete for workouts
- Filter visualisation by week/month
- Add additional metrics (e.g. avg pace)

body:
We just finished implementing DAPO and applied it to training small language models, specifically with `unsloth/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` [here](https://github.com/lavaman131/reasoning-slms) (includes DAPO config usage) and were able to get some positive results as described in my [technical blog](https://alexlavaee.me/projects/reasoning-slms/).

I thought it might be useful to submit a PR in case the TRL community would benefit from a DAPO implementation. I tried to follow the rough structure of the GRPO trainer, but am of course happy to get any feedback on the code.

Here is a rough overview of the proposed API extending off of what the current GRPO API was missing:

* Soft Overlong Punishment

```python
use_soft_overlong_punishment: Optional[bool] = field(
    default=True,
    metadata={
        "help": "A length-aware penalty mechanism designed to shape the reward for truncated samples. According to the "
        "[DAPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.14476) paper, this signals to the model to avoid excessively long responses."
    },
)
soft_punish_cache: Optional[int] = field(
    default=0,
    metadata={
        "help": "The L_cache term in the soft overlong punishnment calculation. According to the "
        "[DAPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.14476) paper, this term determines how close"
        "to the max completion length a response can get before being penalized."
    },
)
```

* Dynamic Sampling

```python
use_dynamic_sampling: Optional[bool] = field(
    default=True,
    metadata={
        "help": "Whether to use dynamic sampling to filter out prompts that have zero variance from the "
        "[DAPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.14476) paper."
    },
)
```
